The page lists TeleBots and Sandworm as actors and gives a long reference list running from 2017 to 2024. One cited headline reports a CIA conclusion, carried by The Washington Post in 2018, that the Russian military was behind the NotPetya attack in Ukraine. Bad Rabbit is described as a suspected variant of Petya. The page names no CVEs.

7e621fd5ba97bd5ae4c19d0f28b0b8e4e0622726.summary: Trend Micro blog post (published 2019-08-07) on Magecart, a digital skimming technique in which malicious JavaScript is placed on e-commerce and payment pages to steal card details during checkout. It describes attacker tactics: infecting third-party code suppliers, automated scanning for unsecured servers, and skimming code reusable across many payment gateways. It cites a $228m UK penalty against British Airways, 17,000 and 962 compromised sites, and a record of 57 payment gateways. The post also promotes Trend Micro Security as the main protection.

7eccc47c8707a8c9363d0829a1a64d0b9d9e5d2a.summary: Fraunhofer FKIE reference entry for the REvil (Sodinokibi) ransomware family. It lists hashes and version-by-version changes from REvil Beta to v1.07, including privilege escalation via CVE-2018-8453, shadow copy deletion, network drive encryption and persistence added in v1.05. It also indexes many third-party reports from 2019 to 2024, including the 2021 Kaseya supply-chain attack.
